statement: This is a navigational summary of the classification used in the species records, not a new phylogenetic analysis. Node counts include descendant species in the archive. Where relationships are contested, the node is marked as disputed.

nodes.label: Dinosauria
nodes.note: The common ancestor of birds and Triceratops, and all its descendants. Birds are living dinosaurs and sit inside this tree, although the archive records only non-avian species.

nodes.label: Saurischia
nodes.note: The lizard-hipped branch, including theropods and sauropodomorphs. The traditional division of Dinosauria into Saurischia and Ornithischia is useful for navigation but does not capture every extinct lineage.

nodes.label: Theropoda
nodes.note: Mostly bipedal dinosaurs, including all known birds. The archive includes predatory, omnivorous and secondarily herbivorous theropods.

nodes.label: Herrerasauria
nodes.note: A group of early saurischians from the Triassic. Their position relative to Theropoda and Sauropodomorpha is debated; some analyses place them outside the two main branches.

nodes.label: Herrerasauridae
nodes.note: Early predatory dinosaurs such as Herrerasaurus. Eoraptor has sometimes been recovered nearby, but its placement remains unresolved and the archive keeps it outside this family; the family’s monophyly and membership are not settled.

nodes.label: Ceratosauria
nodes.note: An early-diverging theropod branch, including Ceratosaurus and the abelisaurids. Many members have short forelimbs and elaborate skull ornament.

nodes.label: Abelisauridae
nodes.note: Short-skulled, often short-armed predators known mainly from the Southern Hemisphere.

nodes.label: Ceratosauridae
nodes.note: A small family of early tetanuran-adjacent theropods, including Ceratosaurus. The wider Ceratosauria also contains the abelisaurids.

nodes.label: Neotheropoda
nodes.note: A broad early theropod grade including coelophysoids and dilophosaurids. The boundary between this grade and Tetanurae is not a single, undisputed character.

nodes.label: Coelophysidae
nodes.note: Slender, long-tailed Triassic and Jurassic theropods such as Coelophysis.

nodes.label: Dilophosauridae
nodes.note: Early theropods with cranial crests, including Dilophosaurus and Cryolophosaurus. Their family-level grouping is debated.

nodes.label: Tetanurae
nodes.note: The large theropod radiation containing megalosauroids, allosauroids, coelurosaurs and birds. The name refers to fused tail vertebrae, but the clade is diagnosed by a combination of characters.

nodes.label: Megalosauroidea
nodes.note: A group of tetanurans including megalosaurids and spinosaurids. Its internal relationships and position relative to allosauroids have changed between analyses.

nodes.label: Spinosauridae
nodes.note: Long-snouted, often fish-focused theropods including Spinosaurus, Baryonyx and Suchomimus.

nodes.label: Megalosauridae
nodes.note: Robust Jurassic tetanurans such as Megalosaurus, Torvosaurus and Eustreptospondylus.

nodes.label: Allosauroidea
nodes.note: A major tetanuran branch containing Allosaurus and the carcharodontosaurids. Some analyses recover a different set of early branches.

nodes.label: Allosauridae
nodes.note: Large Jurassic predators, including Allosaurus.

nodes.label: Carcharodontosauridae
nodes.note: Giant, long-skulled predators with serrated teeth, including Carcharodontosaurus, Giganotosaurus and Acrocanthosaurus.

nodes.label: Metriacanthosauridae
nodes.note: Jurassic allosauroids such as Sinraptor and Monolophosaurus. Their family placement has been unstable.

nodes.label: Coelurosauria
nodes.note: The theropod branch containing tyrannosaurs, compsognathids, ornithomimosaurs, maniraptorans and birds. Many members preserve feathers or feather-like filaments.

nodes.label: Tyrannosauridae
nodes.note: Large, deep-skulled coelurosaurs including Tyrannosaurus, Albertosaurus and Tarbosaurus.

nodes.label: Proceratosauridae
nodes.note: Small to medium early tyrannosauroids with cranial crests, such as Guanlong. Yutyrannus and Dilong are included following analyses that recover them here; other analyses place them outside the family or outside Tyrannosauroidea.

nodes.label: Compsognathidae
nodes.note: Small, lightly built coelurosaurs including Compsognathus and Sinosauropteryx. The family is not recovered by every analysis.

nodes.label: Maniraptora
nodes.note: The clade containing oviraptorosaurs, therizinosaurs, dromaeosaurs, troodontids, birds and their close relatives. Maniraptorans include the only dinosaurs with confirmed flight.

nodes.label: Ornithomimidae
nodes.note: Long-legged, toothless or nearly toothless coelurosaurs such as Gallimimus. Their diet is debated.

nodes.label: Deinocheiridae
nodes.note: Large, unusual ornithomimosaurs including Deinocheirus.

nodes.label: Therizinosauridae
nodes.note: Secondarily herbivorous theropods with large bellies, long forelimbs and prominent claws.

nodes.label: Oviraptoridae
nodes.note: Deep-beaked maniraptorans, several of which are preserved on nests.

nodes.label: Caenagnathidae
nodes.note: Often lightly built oviraptorosaurs, including Gigantoraptor.

nodes.label: Dromaeosauridae
nodes.note: Raptor-like maniraptorans with an enlarged second pedal claw, including Velociraptor, Deinonychus and Microraptor.

nodes.label: Anchiornithidae
nodes.note: Small feathered maniraptorans such as Anchiornis. Their position relative to birds and troodontids is debated.

nodes.label: Scansoriopterygidae
nodes.note: Tiny maniraptorans with elongated hand digits; Yi qi preserves a membranous wing. Their relationships and locomotion are contested.

nodes.label: Sauropodomorpha
nodes.note: The sauropod branch, including early bipedal forms and the giant quadrupedal sauropods.

nodes.label: Plateosauria
nodes.note: Early sauropodomorphs such as Plateosaurus, Massospondylus and Mussaurus. They were mostly facultatively bipedal and much smaller than later sauropods.

nodes.label: Plateosauridae
nodes.note: Large Triassic plateosaurians, including Plateosaurus.

nodes.label: Massospondylidae
nodes.note: Early sauropodomorphs including Massospondylus and Mussaurus, known from eggs and growth series.

nodes.label: Sauropoda
nodes.note: The giant long-necked sauropods. The archive treats the familiar families as navigational groups rather than a complete phylogenetic resolution.

nodes.label: Diplodocidae
nodes.note: Long, low-slung sauropods such as Diplodocus and Apatosaurus.

nodes.label: Dicraeosauridae
nodes.note: Sauropods with relatively short necks and tall, forked neural spines, including Dicraeosaurus and Bajadasaurus.

nodes.label: Rebbachisauridae
nodes.note: Diplodocoid sauropods with broad snouts and rapid tooth replacement, including Nigersaurus.

nodes.label: Brachiosauridae
nodes.note: High-shouldered sauropods with long forelimbs, including Brachiosaurus and Europasaurus.

nodes.label: Camarasauridae
nodes.note: Robust sauropods with deep skulls and spoon-shaped teeth, including Camarasaurus.

nodes.label: Mamenchisauridae
nodes.note: Asian sauropods with exceptionally long necks, including Mamenchisaurus.

nodes.label: Titanosauria
nodes.note: A broad label for the Cretaceous titanosaurs. The archive uses it as a navigational grouping; titanosaur family-level relationships are actively revised.

nodes.label: Saltasauridae
nodes.note: Small to medium titanosaurs, some with dermal armour, including Saltasaurus.

nodes.label: Turiasauria
nodes.note: A European and North American sauropod lineage including Turiasaurus. Its position among eusauropods is debated.

nodes.label: Eusauropoda
nodes.note: A broad grade of sauropods including Shunosaurus and Jobaria. The archive uses it where a finer family assignment is not secure.

nodes.label: Ornithischia
nodes.note: The bird-hipped dinosaurs, including armoured forms, ornithopods and marginocephalians. The name refers to the shape of the pelvis, not to a close relationship with birds.

nodes.label: Thyreophora
nodes.note: Armoured ornithischians, including stegosaurs, ankylosaurs and early forms such as Scelidosaurus.

nodes.label: Stegosauria
nodes.note: Plated and spiked thyreophorans. The archive's stegosaurs are grouped in Stegosauridae; the arrangement of their plates and spikes varies between species.

nodes.label: Stegosauridae
nodes.note: The main stegosaur family, including Stegosaurus and Kentrosaurus.

nodes.label: Ankylosauria
nodes.note: Armoured thyreophorans with broad bodies and osteoderms. Some have tail clubs; others do not.

nodes.label: Ankylosauridae
nodes.note: Ankylosaurs with fused skull armour and, in most members, a tail club.

nodes.label: Nodosauridae
nodes.note: Ankylosaurs with narrow skulls, prominent shoulder spines and no tail club.

nodes.label: Scelidosauridae
nodes.note: Early armoured dinosaurs such as Scelidosaurus, outside the ankylosaur-stegosaur split.

nodes.label: Neornithischia
nodes.note: A broad ornithischian branch containing ornithopods and marginocephalians. Small early forms such as Lesothosaurus and Heterodontosaurus are included here.

nodes.label: Heterodontosauridae
nodes.note: Small early ornithischians with heterodont dentition, including Heterodontosaurus.

nodes.label: Lesothosauridae
nodes.note: Small, lightly built Early Jurassic ornithischians such as Lesothosaurus.

nodes.label: Ornithopoda
nodes.note: Bipedal or facultatively quadrupedal herbivores, including iguanodontians and hadrosaurs. Many later forms evolved extensive dental batteries.

nodes.label: Iguanodontidae
nodes.note: A broad family-level grouping for Iguanodon and its close relatives. The boundary with hadrosaurs is not sharp in every analysis.

nodes.label: Hadrosauridae
nodes.note: Duck-billed dinosaurs with complex dental batteries and, in many species, hollow cranial crests.

nodes.label: Marginocephalia
nodes.note: The clade containing ceratopsians and pachycephalosaurs. Both groups have a shelf at the back of the skull, but their body plans are very different.

nodes.label: Ceratopsia
nodes.note: Beaked herbivores with a frill in later members. Early forms such as Psittacosaurus and Protoceratops lack the large horns of derived ceratopsids.

nodes.label: Ceratopsidae
nodes.note: Large, horned ceratopsians. The archive groups them at family level rather than forcing every specimen into a subfamily.

nodes.label: Pachycephalosauria
nodes.note: Bipedal herbivores with thickened skull roofs. The dome's function is debated; the archive does not treat head-butting as established.

nodes.label: Pachycephalosauridae
nodes.note: The main pachycephalosaur family, including Pachycephalosaurus.

nodes.label: Huayangosauridae
nodes.note: Basal stegosaurs including Huayangosaurus and Gigantspinosaurus; the position of Gigantspinosaurus varies between analyses.

nodes.label: Protoceratopsidae
nodes.note: Small ceratopsians without the large facial horns of Ceratopsidae, including Protoceratops.

nodes.label: Psittacosauridae
nodes.note: Early ceratopsians with parrot-like beaks; Psittacosaurus is the principal genus.

nodes.label: Tenontosauridae
nodes.note: Robust iguanodontians including Tenontosaurus; separated here from the broader Iguanodontidae.

nodes.label: Dryosauridae
nodes.note: Small bipedal iguanodontians including Dryosaurus.

nodes.label: Camptosauridae
nodes.note: Basal ankylopollexians including Camptosaurus.

nodes.label: Hypsilophodontidae
nodes.note: Small bipedal ornithopods. Recent analyses restrict the family to Hypsilophodon and close relatives; older treatments used it as a wastebasket for many small ornithopods.

nodes.label: Thescelosauridae
nodes.note: Basal neornithischians including Orodromeus; their position relative to other ornithopods varies.

nodes.label: Rhabdodontidae
nodes.note: Robust European ornithopods including Rhabdodon.

nodes.label: Ornithopoda incertae sedis
nodes.note: Ornithopods whose family placement is unresolved, including Leaellynasaura.

nodes.label: Ankylosauria incertae sedis
nodes.note: Ankylosaurs whose family placement is unresolved, including Minmi.

nodes.label: Saurischia incertae sedis
nodes.note: Early saurischians whose position is unresolved, including Eoraptor.
